registered_by: executor seat, on E08-shot, before the first submission of any E08 graph
how_these_were_chosen: The date as a plain integer with a run index appended, continuing the rule specs/E09-seeds.json and specs/E09-A3-seeds.json use: 2026-08-12 runs 11, 12 and 13. The property that matters is that every number is fixed BEFORE any result is seen, and a date-derived seed is checkable against this file's own git timestamp. No seed here was drawn from a prior run, from any served template, or from anything this seat had already looked at.

allocation.2026081211: the probe — the one generation this wave authorises up front
allocation.2026081212: reserve 1, spendable only on a named cause the probe surfaces

why_the_index_starts_at_11_rather_than_0: specs/E09-A3-seeds.json already registered 2026081201 and 2026081202 on the same calendar day, and both were spent or reserved against the E09 clean-chain trajectory. Reusing either number here would put a seed registered for one experiment onto another, and the record would afterwards have to explain which run a number belonged to. The offset keeps every seed on this rig traceable to exactly one registration.
ceiling: 3 generations in wave 1 — 1 probe plus 2 reserve. Gate C arms on the measured billing number from estimate_credits, recorded before the first submission, and halts before any submission that would exceed the ceiling. Spent credits have no compensator; the bound is the honest treatment.
binds_in_both_directions: An experiment that pre-registered seeds must use one of them, and an experiment that pre-registered none may not vary its seed at all. tools/armature_core/gates.py::gate_s_seed_registration enforces both clauses at build time and tools/armature_core/route_gates.py::gate_s_registration enforces them again against the graph that is about to run.
